newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady, instances $1.00-$2.00 per cwt lower, according to USDA's weekly National Rice Market Summary.
Long grain milled rice prices sold mostly at $20.00; medium grain traded mostly at $18.00-$19.00; second heads were steady and brewers were steady in tight supply.

Rice by-products were lower, bran was steady to $5.00 lower in Arkansas, $8.00-$12.00 lower in Louisiana, and untested in Texas. Millfeed was mostly steady to $5.00 lower except in Arkansas where prices were $8.00-$11.00 lower.
In California, rice prices were steady with medium grain selling mostly from $18.00-$19.00, second heads were steady, bran was $5.00 lower.
For the week ended July 12 there were no ship loadings.
For the week ending June 28, 1997, the Port of Sacramento loaded the Parinda Naree with 20,891 mt of U.S. No. 1 medium graiin milled rice destined for Turkey, not 10,445 mt as perviously reported.
Inspections of California rice for export for the week ending July 12: There were no rice inspections.

On June 28th there were 460,772 cwt of medium grain milled rice inspected, not 230,375 as previously reported. The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 9,937,247 cwt compared to 6,992,387 cwt a year ago.
Feed by-products prices (dollars per short ton, FOB mills).
